props.text: The project needs to record its architectural decisions.
props.quote: We need to record the architectural decisions made on this project

props.text: Defining each EKS resource in a custom module requires significant effort.
props.quote: Defining each resource in our own Terraform module maximises flexibility but also requires a significant level of effort

props.text: The existing Terraform registry EKS module optimizes for speed of delivery.
props.quote: We could instead make use of the [existing Terraform registry EKS module](https://registry.terraform.io/modules/terraform-aws-modules/eks/aws/latest) to optimise for speed of delivery

props.text: Many module defaults are fine for the team's purposes for the foreseeable future.
props.quote:
We can define fully configured EKS clusters quickly and easily, because many module defaults will be fine for our purposes 
for the foreseeable future

props.text: The EKS module has comprehensive support for many EKS cluster configuration options.
props.quote: The EKS module has comprehensive support for many of the options for EKS cluster config (e.g. worker node types)

props.text: Terraform providers are not nodes in the plan graph, so AWS resources are not guaranteed to be created before the Kubernetes provider initializes.
props.quote:
Terraform providers are not handled as nodes in the Terraform plan graph, so Terraform cannot guarantee that AWS resources 
are fully created at the point that it configures the `kubernetes` provider

props.text: The Kubernetes provider requires arguments that depend on AWS resource outputs, causing race conditions in a single state.
props.quote:
The `kubernetes` provider requires arguments that are dependent on AWS resource 
outputs, so a naïve implementation would look like this:

props.text: Terraform cannot include AWS load balancers provisioned by Kubernetes services in its destruction plan, preventing EKS cluster deletion.
props.quote:
Ingress controllers and Kubernetes 
`Service` objects commonly provision AWS load balancers that Terraform does not know about, and therefore cannot include 
in a destruction plan

props.text: The separation keeps generic cluster infrastructure distinct from GOV.UK-specific configuration, allowing for future cluster switching.
props.quote:
This is an important and useful separation to enforce, because it keeps the largely 
generic cluster infrastructure separate from the GOV.UK-specific configuration and supporting services

props.text: The project requires an AWS load balancer in front of the cluster to avoid direct internet exposure.
props.quote:
We do not want to expose the cluster directly to the internet, so we require an AWS load balancer in front of the
cluster

props.text: The load balancer must support TLS termination and integration with AWS Route 53.
props.quote: The load balancer must support TLS termination and integration with our DNS provider (AWS Route 53)

props.text: Built-in Kubernetes cloud providers are deprecated in favor of out-of-tree providers.
props.quote:
Built-in cloud providers are now [considered deprecated overall, in favour of out-of-tree providers](https://kubernetes.io/blog/2019/04/17/the-future-of-cloud-providers-in-kubernetes/),
so users are now required to use an [Ingress Controller](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/ingress-controllers/) 
with support for `Service` resources

props.text: The AWS Load Balancer Controller is the primary and recommended ingress controller for AWS EKS.
props.quote:
The primary, and recommended, ingress controller for AWS' Elastic Kubernetes Service (EKS) is
the [AWS Load Balancer Controller](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/userguide/aws-load-balancer-controller.html), which can provision and manage [ALBs for `Ingress` resources and NLBs for
`Service` resources](https://kubernetes-sigs.github.io/aws-load-balancer-controller/v2.2/#aws-load-balancer-controller)

props.text: Kubernetes has a 4-month release cycle, making frequent upgrades necessary.
props.quote: Kubernetes has a 4-month release cycle, so upgrades will be relatively frequent

props.text: The team requires a robust and mature node upgrade process due to the destructive nature of worker updates.
props.quote:
We will require a robust and mature node upgrade 
process, given the potentially destructive nature of worker updates

props.text: The requirements for worker nodes are not fully known, making flexibility important.
props.quote: At this stage our requirements for worker nodes are not fully known, so maintaining flexibility is important

props.text: Managed node groups handle graceful upgrades largely automatically, unlike self-managed groups.
props.quote: Managed node groups handle graceful upgrades largely automatically

props.text: The team requires a way to define Kubernetes resources as installable packages with configuration options passed at deploy time.
props.quote:
At a high level, we require a means to define an application's Kubernetes resources as an installable 
package, with configuration options passed in at deploy time

props.text: The team uses Terraform for AWS infrastructure management and wants to maintain a strict separation of concerns between infrastructure and application management.
props.quote:
We are currently using Terraform for AWS infrastructure management, and we should maintain a strict separation of
concerns between managing cloud infrastructure and the software applications that run on top

props.text: Helm has widespread industry adoption, a large number of existing packages, and support in the wider devops and development ecosystem.
props.quote:
Helm by comparison has widespread industry adoption,
a [large number of existing packages](https://artifacthub.io/packages/search), and widespread support in the wider
devops and development ecosystem

props.text: The sidecar pattern does not meet the need for logging as a default service for all containers
props.quote:
We must have logging as a service and enable it by default for all containers, so the sidecar pattern does not meet
our needs

props.text: The logging agent must annotate and index logs with Kubernetes cluster metadata
props.quote:
To make application logs searchable and navigable, we require the logging agent to annotate and index logs with
Kubernetes cluster metadata (namespace, pod name, labels, and so on)

props.text: Elasticsearch and Kibana are chosen due to their extensive support for this use case and ecosystem
props.quote:
For now, the obvious choice is Elasticsearch and Kibana, due to their extensive support for this use case and in this
ecosystem

props.text: Deploying a local logging service ensures usability sooner and familiarity with Kubernetes logging details
props.quote:
Doing so will ensure we have a usable logging service for our users sooner rather than later, and 
get familiar with the details of logging within Kubernetes ourselves

props.text: The team wants to reconstitute the full state of a running cluster from an external source of truth.
props.quote:
We want
to do this because we want the ability to reconstitute the full state of a running cluster from an external source of truth

props.text: Managing sensitive configuration in Git repositories presents significant challenges and pain points.
props.quote:
there are significant challenges and pain points when
managing sensitive config in Git repositories

props.text: The team must maintain end-to-end encryption of secrets until a running container uses them.
props.quote:
We must maintain end-to-end encryption of secrets, up until the point a running container uses a secret, where Kubernetes
must necessarily decrypt the secret for use

props.text: The team must support automatic propagation of secret rotations from AWS to services in the cluster.
props.quote:
We must be able to support rotation of secrets in AWS SecretsManager, where a change of value in AWS is automatically
propagated to services in the cluster

props.text: Prometheus and Alertmanager lack built-in web authentication, requiring authentication at the load balancer level.
props.quote:
Prometheus and Alertmanager do not support any form of web-based user authentication, so authentication must happen at a
proxy or load balancer in front of the application

props.text: The AWS Load Balancer Controller supports OIDC authentication, which is required for the infrastructure.
props.quote:
We are currently using Application Load Balancers (ALB) in front of Prometheus and Alertmanager, from
the [AWS Load Balancer Controller](0004-use-aws-load-balancer-controller-for-edge-traffic-services.md), which
supports [authentication with AWS Cognito or OIDC-compliant identity providers](https://kubernetes-sigs.github.io/aws-load-balancer-controller/v2.3/guide/ingress/annotations/#authentication)

props.text: GitHub does not support OIDC, and AWS Cognito does not support OAuth2, preventing direct integration between them.
props.quote:
GitHub as an identity provider does not support OIDC, only OAuth2, so we cannot use it for ALB authentication. AWS
Cognito [does not support OAuth2, only OIDC](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cognito/latest/developerguide/cognito-identity.html),
so we cannot use it with GitHub as an identity provider

props.text: Argo CD already includes Dex as an OIDC-compliant identity broker.
props.quote:
ArgoCD, our current CD tool,
also [implements authentication with OIDC](https://argo-cd.readthedocs.io/en/stable/operator-manual/user-management/#existing-oidc-provider),
and [includes an OIDC-compliant identity broker](https://argoproj.github.io/argo-workflows/argo-server-sso-argocd/): [Dex](https://dexidp.io)

props.text: Systems like Google's Safe Browsing might flag a Non-GOV.UK domain as a phishing site if it looks like a GOV.UK site or plays a publicly detectable role in serving content.
props.quote:
In either case, systems such as [Google's Safe Browsing](https://transparencyreport.google.com/safe-browsing/search),
in use by browsers to automatically block requests to dangerous sites, might flag the domain as a phishing site

props.text: Such flagging could cause a major incident, making large parts of GOV.UK inaccessible.
props.quote:
At worst, this could
cause a major incident, making large parts of GOV.UK inaccessible

props.text: Kubernetes HPAs currently scale only on CPU and memory metrics from metrics-server
props.quote: Kubernetes Horizontal Pod Autoscalers (HPAs) on GOV.UK currently scale only on CPU and memory metrics from `metrics-server

props.text: Workloads need to scale on application-level signals such as Sidekiq queue backlog length
props.quote: Several workloads (starting with Chat AI) need to scale on application-level signals, such as a Sidekiq queue backlog length

props.text: Kubernetes requires external signals to be available through the external.metrics.k8s.io API group
props.quote: Kubernetes requires these signals to be available through the `external.metrics.k8s.io` API group

props.text: Prometheus already scrapes the backlog metric in every cluster but lacks a component to translate it to the external-metrics API
props.quote:
Prometheus already scrapes the backlog metric (`sidekiq_queue_backlog{job="govuk-chat-worker"}`) in every cluster, but
the cluster lacks a component that translates Prometheus data into the `external-metrics` API

props.text: Terraform Cloud's cost and proprietary lock-in are no longer acceptable to the team.
props.quote:
its cost and
proprietary lock‑in are no longer acceptable

props.text: A renewal decision for the Terraform Cloud service is due within six months.
props.quote: A renewal decision is due within six months

props.text: S3-backed state with S3 native locking has matured.
props.quote: S3‑backed state with S3 native locking has matured

props.text: AWS already meets the organization's security baseline.
props.quote: AWS already meets our security baseline

props.text: The team aims to adhere to the principle of least privilege by providing specific IAM and Kubernetes roles.
props.quote: We aim to adhere to the principle of least privilege wherever we can

props.text: The lowest level of privilege should not be capable of causing a production outage.
props.quote: we felt that the lowest level of privilege should not be capable of causing a production outage

props.text: Developers need a role to look around without changing anything.
props.quote: Developers wanting to just look about without changing anything

props.text: Junior or apprentice level roles need access without the ability to accidentally change anything.
props.quote: Junior/apprentice level roles needing access without the ability to accidentally change anything

props.text: Compromised IAM access keys pose a significant security risk.
props.quote:
If these keys are compromised through leakage or reuse by unauthorised actors, they can pose a significant
security risk

props.text: Long-lived keys increase security risk.
props.quote: Long-lived keys increase this risk, and regular rotation is encouraged to mitigate it

props.text: Many third-party services support the use of IAM roles.
props.quote: Many third-party services now support the use of IAM roles

props.text: Internal applications can use Kubernetes Pod identities or assume IAM roles directly.
props.quote:
Where possible, these applications (or their Kubernetes pods) should use Kubernetes `Pod` identities or assume IAM roles
directly, rather than relying on access keys

props.text: The existing CI/CD implementation has security flaws and causes incidents
props.quote:
An IT Health Check carried out in 2024 identified security flaws in the implementation of the deployment process. This, 
and a number of incidents directly caused by this process, and the team's ongoing issues with Argo Workflows has led us 
to want to re-engineer our CI/CD pipelines

props.text: The team is moving away from Terraform Cloud and needs a replacement for applying Terraform code
props.quote:
An additional, contributing factor for making the decision was [ADR 0014](./0014-replace-terraform-cloud.md), in which we
decided we would move away from Terraform Cloud. To do so will require us to have a replacement for automatically applying
Terraform code in different environments

props.text: The team does not want to rely on undocumented features in alternative tools
props.quote:
We did not want to rely on undocumented features, so we opted to prototype a workaround for the problem with Argo 
Rollouts to see how it would look and feel

props.text: The team prefers not to run virtual machines to avoid additional infrastructure support
props.quote:
We discussed the implications of running EC2 instances versus running Concourse in the Kubernetes 
clusters, and we decided that we should stay away from running virtual machines. It adds additional infrastructure for 
us to support long term, which is different from everything else we support

props.text: The existing generic Helm chart has become complex, hard to navigate, and difficult to maintain due to embedded Golang templates and variable dependencies.
props.quote:
For us, as a
Platform Engineering team, this had led to a code base that:

* has lots of Golang templates embedded in YAML,
* has lots of importing and variable values derived from other variables,
* is hard to navigate,
* is hard to reason about,
* is hard to change,
* and is easy to get wrong

props.text: Application teams lack the deep Kubernetes and infrastructure knowledge required to manage resources directly, which the Platform Engineering team possesses.
props.quote:
Knowing what resources you need, their configuration, and how their interrelations
requires a good amount of Kubernetes knowledge, and knowledge of the rest of your infrastructure. This knowledge is 
readily available within the Platform Engineering team, but less so among the application teams we serve

props.text: The team intends to use Crossplane to create a higher-level API that abstracts resource types for users, simplifying deployment standardization.
props.quote:
We have decided that we want to use Crossplane to create a Kubernetes-flavoured API for our users. The API will abstract
the types of resources our users need to create at a higher level than offered by the standard Kubernetes API

props.text: The team plans to use Crossplane to manage backing services within Kubernetes, eventually replacing the current use of Terraform for this purpose.
props.quote:
We plan to use this feature to create a catalogue of backing services our users can get access to through Kubernetes. 
This will eventually replace creating application backing services in Terraform

props.text: The team requires the ability to perform automated testing of policies in isolation of a full Kubernetes cluster.
props.quote:
The single other requirement we set ourselves for choosing a tool was the ability to perform automated testing of the 
policies in isolation of a full Kubernetes cluster

props.text: OPA Gatekeeper is a mature CNCF graduated project with good adoption among other Kubernetes users.
props.quote:
We have chosen to adopt OPA Gatekeeper for applying policy to Kubernetes objects because it is a mature CNCF graduated 
project with good adoption among other Kubernetes users

props.text: The team has members with strong, positive open source experience of running and working with OPA Gatekeeper.
props.quote:
We also have a number people in the team at the time we've made the decision with strong, positive, open source 
experience of running and working with OPA Gatekeeper
